facts.text: Dinner's on me tonight, Don. Just promise you won't make me rehearse the dance again before dessert.
facts.why: Hannah never says this. In the film it is Don who sets up the private dinner at his apartment, and Hannah is the one who accuses him of treating it like a rehearsal. Her real line about fruit is a good fit.
The act is billed Hannah and Hewes in the plot, and Don asks for Miss Brown by her real name. No Hewes and Brown studio appears.

facts.text: Don and Hannah in tramp's rags, singing about dinner with the Vanderbilts.
facts.why: In A Couple of Swells the two play tramps and the Vanderbilts have asked them up for tea. There is no dinner in the number.
facts.fix: Don and Hannah in tramp's rags, invited to tea with the Vanderbilts.

vibe.verdict: A cinema snack bar that is fine but generic, with a studio name that is not quite right and none of the film's sweets.
missing: The chocolate egg, flowers and live bunny in a top hat that arrive at Don's apartment (the finale)
'Can you drown a brunette in this?' at the bar (Don and Mike)
Don drumming in the toy store: 'Drum Crazy' (the opening)
Peach or lemon: 'she has to be a peach' and 'I suppose I'm a lemon!' (Don and Hannah)
'Snookie-Ookums' and 'I Love a Piano' (the Hannah and Hewes act)
Don's private dinner at his apartment (Hannah arrives)
ideas: Swap 'Hot cross bun bread and butter pudding' note for 'Chocolate egg and bunny in a top hat'.
Swap 'Easter bonnet pink fizz punch' for 'Peach and lemon fizz', from the peach and lemon lines.
Swap 'Manhattan with a cherry' note for 'Can you drown a brunette in this?'
